text.p: - Central bank governors from Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Macedonia on Monday agreed on succession of former Yugoslavia's assests according to the proposal of the Bank of International Settlements.
- Workers of machine-producer Litostroj finished their strike on Monday after Joze Duhovnik, the general manager of Litostroj, resigned.

- Border tunnel between Slovenia and Austria will be open for traffic by the end of October. Total reconstruction of the tunnel is expected to begin in March 1997 and would cost Slovenia about 240 million tolars ($1.8 million).
- Slovenia's electoral campaign will start on October 10, one month before scheduled general elections.
- Experts from America and Europe on Monday started the first international workshop on environmental studies. The ecological project will last five years.
- Estonian Foreign Minister Siim Kallas visited his Slovenian counterpart Davorin Kracun, and Defence Minister Jelko Kacin and Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Monday.

- Delegation of 25 bankers and businessmen from Switzerland attended a business conference with Slovenian businessmen in Ljubljana on Monday. They discussed possibilities for economic cooperation between the two countries.
- Average gross salary in July rose 3.8 percent to 131,803 tolars ($976.3), Slovenia's Statistical Office reported on Monday.
